UPSTREAM: cpu/x86/smm: Fix explicit 'addr32' usage in clang builds The addr32 prefix is required by binutils, because even when given an explicit address which is greater than 64KiB, it will throw a warning about truncation, and stupidly emit the opcode with a 16-bit addressing mode and the wrong address. However, in the case of LLVM, this doesn't happen, and is happy to just use 32-bit addressing whenever it may require it. This means that LLVM never really needs an explicit addr32 prefix to use 32-bit addressing in 16-bit mode.
